You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\\n\\n# Python Testing with pytest\\n\\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`\'s `assertEqual` zoo.\\n\\n## Structure and naming\\n\\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\\n\\n## Fixtures over setUp\\n\\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\\n\\n```python\\nimport pytest\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef settings(tmp_path):\\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \\"test.db\\"))\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef repo(settings):\\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\\n    run_migrations(conn)\\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\\n    conn.close()\\n```\\n\\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\\n\\n## Parametrize instead of loops\\n\\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\\n\\n```python\\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\\n    (\\"title_a\\", \\"title_b\\", \\"expected\\"),\\n    [\\n        (\\"Song (Live)\\", \\"Song\\", True),\\n        (\\"Song\\", \\"Totally Other\\", False),\\n    ],\\n    ids=[\\"live-suffix-matches\\", \\"different-titles-reject\\"],\\n)\\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\\n```\\n\\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\\n\\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \\"auto\\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\\nasyncio_mode = \\"auto\\"\\n```\\n\\n```python\\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\\"items\\": []})\\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\\"abc\\")\\n    assert result == []\\n```\\n\\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\\n\\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\\n\\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr\'s web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\\n\\n```python\\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \\"get_playlist\\", boom)\\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\\n```\\n\\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`\'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\\n\\n## Coverage and CI\\n\\n```bash\\npytest                       # all tests\\npytest -k \\"match and not slow\\"   # filter by name expression\\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\\n```\\n\\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\\n\\n## Targeted mutation testing\\n\\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\\n\\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\\n\\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository\'s pinned environment. Check the installed version\'s help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\\n\\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\\n\\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\\n\\n## Common mistakes\\n\\n| Mistake | Fix |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \\"auto\\"` or mark it. |\\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn\'t awaitable. |\\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. {'state': 'available', 'value': {'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': '<skill_content name="python-testing">\n# Skill: python-testing\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\n\n# Python Testing with pytest\n\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`\'s `assertEqual` zoo.\n\n## Structure and naming\n\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\n\n## Fixtures over setUp\n\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef settings(tmp_path):\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / "test.db"))\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef repo(settings):\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\n    run_migrations(conn)\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\n    conn.close()\n```\n\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\n\n## Parametrize instead of loops\n\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\n\n```python\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    ("title_a", "title_b", "expected"),\n    [\n        ("Song (Live)", "Song", True),\n        ("Song", "Totally Other", False),\n    ],\n    ids=["live-suffix-matches", "different-titles-reject"],\n)\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\n```\n\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\n\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = "auto"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\n\n```toml\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\nasyncio_mode = "auto"\n```\n\n```python\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={"items": []})\n    result = await client.get_playlist("abc")\n    assert result == []\n```\n\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\n\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\n\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr\'s web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\n\n```python\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, "get_playlist", boom)\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\n```\n\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`\'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\n\n## Coverage and CI\n\n```bash\npytest                       # all tests\npytest -k "match and not slow"   # filter by name expression\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\n```\n\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\n\n## Targeted mutation testing\n\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\n\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\n\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository\'s pinned environment. Check the installed version\'s help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\n\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\n\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\\n\\n# Python Testing with pytest\\n\\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\\n\\n## Structure and naming\\n\\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\\n\\n## Fixtures over setUp\\n\\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\\n\\n```python\\nimport pytest\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef settings(tmp_path):\\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \\\"test.db\\\"))\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef repo(settings):\\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\\n    run_migrations(conn)\\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\\n    conn.close()\\n```\\n\\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\\n\\n## Parametrize instead of loops\\n\\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\\n\\n```python\\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\\n    (\\\"title_a\\\", \\\"title_b\\\", \\\"expected\\\"),\\n    [\\n        (\\\"Song (Live)\\\", \\\"Song\\\", True),\\n        (\\\"Song\\\", \\\"Totally Other\\\", False),\\n    ],\\n    ids=[\\\"live-suffix-matches\\\", \\\"different-titles-reject\\\"],\\n)\\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\\n```\\n\\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\\n\\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\\nasyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"\\n```\\n\\n```python\\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\\\"items\\\": []})\\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\\\"abc\\\")\\n    assert result == []\\n```\\n\\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\\n\\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\\n\\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\\n\\n```python\\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \\\"get_playlist\\\", boom)\\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\\n```\\n\\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\\n\\n## Coverage and CI\\n\\n```bash\\npytest                       # all tests\\npytest -k \\\"match and not slow\\\"   # filter by name expression\\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\\n```\\n\\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\\n\\n## Targeted mutation testing\\n\\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\\n\\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\\n\\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\\n\\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\\n\\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\\n\\n## Common mistakes\\n\\n| Mistake | Fix |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors.                           "type": "text",
                          "text": "<skill_content name=\"python-testing\">\n# Skill: python-testing\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\n\n# Python Testing with pytest\n\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\n\n## Structure and naming\n\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\n\n## Fixtures over setUp\n\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef settings(tmp_path):\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \"test.db\"))\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef repo(settings):\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\n    run_migrations(conn)\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\n    conn.close()\n```\n\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\n\n## Parametrize instead of loops\n\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\n\n```python\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"title_a\", \"title_b\", \"expected\"),\n    [\n        (\"Song (Live)\", \"Song\", True),\n        (\"Song\", \"Totally Other\", False),\n    ],\n    ids=[\"live-suffix-matches\", \"different-titles-reject\"],\n)\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\n```\n\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\n\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\n\n```toml\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\nasyncio_mode = \"auto\"\n```\n\n```python\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\"items\": []})\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\"abc\")\n    assert result == []\n```\n\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\n\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\n\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\n\n```python\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \"get_playlist\", boom)\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\n```\n\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\n\n## Coverage and CI\n\n```bash\npytest                       # all tests\npytest -k \"match and not slow\"   # filter by name expression\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\n```\n\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\n\n## Targeted mutation testing\n\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\n\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\n\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\n\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\n\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` or mark it. |\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\n\n## References\n\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

                    "text": "<skill_content name=\"python-testing\">\n# Skill: python-testing\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\n\n# Python Testing with pytest\n\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\n\n## Structure and naming\n\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\n\n## Fixtures over setUp\n\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef settings(tmp_path):\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \"test.db\"))\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef repo(settings):\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\n    run_migrations(conn)\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\n    conn.close()\n```\n\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\n\n## Parametrize instead of loops\n\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\n\n```python\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"title_a\", \"title_b\", \"expected\"),\n    [\n        (\"Song (Live)\", \"Song\", True),\n        (\"Song\", \"Totally Other\", False),\n    ],\n    ids=[\"live-suffix-matches\", \"different-titles-reject\"],\n)\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\n```\n\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\n\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\n\n```toml\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\nasyncio_mode = \"auto\"\n```\n\n```python\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\"items\": []})\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\"abc\")\n    assert result == []\n```\n\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\n\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\n\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\n\n```python\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \"get_playlist\", boom)\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\n```\n\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\n\n## Coverage and CI\n\n```bash\npytest                       # all tests\npytest -k \"match and not slow\"   # filter by name expression\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\n```\n\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\n\n## Targeted mutation testing\n\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\n\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\n\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\n\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\n\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` or mark it. |\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\n\n## References\n\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\\n\\n# Python Testing with pytest\\n\\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\\n\\n## Structure and naming\\n\\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\\n\\n## Fixtures over setUp\\n\\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\\n\\n```python\\nimport pytest\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef settings(tmp_path):\\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \\\"test.db\\\"))\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef repo(settings):\\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\\n    run_migrations(conn)\\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\\n    conn.close()\\n```\\n\\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\\n\\n## Parametrize instead of loops\\n\\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\\n\\n```python\\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\\n    (\\\"title_a\\\", \\\"title_b\\\", \\\"expected\\\"),\\n    [\\n        (\\\"Song (Live)\\\", \\\"Song\\\", True),\\n        (\\\"Song\\\", \\\"Totally Other\\\", False),\\n    ],\\n    ids=[\\\"live-suffix-matches\\\", \\\"different-titles-reject\\\"],\\n)\\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\\n```\\n\\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\\n\\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\\nasyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"\\n```\\n\\n```python\\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\\\"items\\\": []})\\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\\\"abc\\\")\\n    assert result == []\\n```\\n\\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\\n\\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\\n\\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\\n\\n```python\\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \\\"get_playlist\\\", boom)\\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\\n```\\n\\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\\n\\n## Coverage and CI\\n\\n```bash\\npytest                       # all tests\\npytest -k \\\"match and not slow\\\"   # filter by name expression\\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\\n```\\n\\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\\n\\n## Targeted mutation testing\\n\\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\\n\\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\\n\\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project.                                 "text": "<skill_content name=\"python-testing\">\n# Skill: python-testing\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\n\n# Python Testing with pytest\n\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\n\n## Structure and naming\n\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\n\n## Fixtures over setUp\n\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef settings(tmp_path):\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \"test.db\"))\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef repo(settings):\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\n    run_migrations(conn)\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\n    conn.close()\n```\n\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\n\n## Parametrize instead of loops\n\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\n\n```python\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"title_a\", \"title_b\", \"expected\"),\n    [\n        (\"Song (Live)\", \"Song\", True),\n        (\"Song\", \"Totally Other\", False),\n    ],\n    ids=[\"live-suffix-matches\", \"different-titles-reject\"],\n)\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\n```\n\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\n\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\n\n```toml\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\nasyncio_mode = \"auto\"\n```\n\n```python\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\"items\": []})\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\"abc\")\n    assert result == []\n```\n\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\n\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\n\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\n\n```python\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \"get_playlist\", boom)\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\n```\n\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\n\n## Coverage and CI\n\n```bash\npytest                       # all tests\npytest -k \"match and not slow\"   # filter by name expression\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\n```\n\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\n\n## Targeted mutation testing\n\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\n\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\n\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\n\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\n\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` or mark it. |\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\n\n## References\n\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\n\n```python\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \"get_playlist\", boom)\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\n```\n\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\n\n## Coverage and CI\n\n```bash\npytest                       # all tests\npytest -k \"match and not slow\"   # filter by name expression\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\n```\n\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\n\n## Targeted mutation testing\n\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\n\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\n\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\n\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\n\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` or mark it. |\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\n\n## References\n\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"

You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\\n\\n# Python Testing with pytest\\n\\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`\'s `assertEqual` zoo.\\n\\n## Structure and naming\\n\\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\\n\\n## Fixtures over setUp\\n\\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\\n\\n```python\\nimport pytest\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef settings(tmp_path):\\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \\"test.db\\"))\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef repo(settings):\\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\\n    run_migrations(conn)\\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\\n    conn.close()\\n```\\n\\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\\n\\n## Parametrize instead of loops\\n\\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\\n\\n```python\\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\\n    (\\"title_a\\", \\"title_b\\", \\"expected\\"),\\n    [\\n        (\\"Song (Live)\\", \\"Song\\", True),\\n        (\\"Song\\", \\"Totally Other\\", False),\\n    ],\\n    ids=[\\"live-suffix-matches\\", \\"different-titles-reject\\"],\\n)\\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\\n```\\n\\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\\n\\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \\"auto\\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\\nasyncio_mode = \\"auto\\"\\n```\\n\\n```python\\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\\"items\\": []})\\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\\"abc\\")\\n    assert result == []\\n```\\n\\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\\n\\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\\n\\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr\'s web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\\n\\n```python\\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \\"get_playlist\\", boom)\\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\\n```\\n\\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`\'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\\n\\n## Coverage and CI\\n\\n```bash\\npytest                       # all tests\\npytest -k \\"match and not slow\\"   # filter by name expression\\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\\n```\\n\\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\\n\\n## Targeted mutation testing\\n\\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\\n\\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\\n\\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository\'s pinned environment. Check the installed version\'s help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\\n\\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\\n\\n# Python Testing with pytest\\n\\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\\n\\n## Structure and naming\\n\\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\\n\\n## Fixtures over setUp\\n\\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\\n\\n```python\\nimport pytest\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef settings(tmp_path):\\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \\\"test.db\\\"))\\n\\n@pytest.fixture\\ndef repo(settings):\\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\\n    run_migrations(conn)\\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\\n    conn.close()\\n```\\n\\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\\n\\n## Parametrize instead of loops\\n\\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\\n\\n```python\\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\\n    (\\\"title_a\\\", \\\"title_b\\\", \\\"expected\\\"),\\n    [\\n        (\\\"Song (Live)\\\", \\\"Song\\\", True),\\n        (\\\"Song\\\", \\\"Totally Other\\\", False),\\n    ],\\n    ids=[\\\"live-suffix-matches\\\", \\\"different-titles-reject\\\"],\\n)\\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\\n```\\n\\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\\n\\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\\n\\n```toml\\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\\nasyncio_mode = \\\"auto\\\"\\n```\\n\\n```python\\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\\\"items\\\": []})\\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\\\"abc\\\")\\n    assert result == []\\n```\\n\\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\\n\\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\\n\\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\\n\\n```python\\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \\\"get_playlist\\\", boom)\\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\\n```\\n\\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\\n\\n## Coverage and CI\\n\\n```bash\\npytest                       # all tests\\npytest -k \\\"match and not slow\\\"   # filter by name expression\\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\\n```\\n\\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\\n\\n## Targeted mutation testing\\n\\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\\n\\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\\n\\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\\n\\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\\n\\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\\n\\n## Common mistakes\\n\\n| Mistake | Fix |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors.                     "type": "text",
                    "text": "<skill_content name=\"python-testing\">\n# Skill: python-testing\n\n> Pair with `python-common-practice` for shared verification guidance.\n\n**Persona:** You are a Python engineer who treats tests as executable specifications. You write tests to constrain behavior, not to chase a coverage number.\n\n# Python Testing with pytest\n\nTests pin behavior. A good test fails for exactly one reason and names that reason. Prefer plain `assert` (pytest rewrites it for rich diffs) over `unittest`'s `assertEqual` zoo.\n\n## Structure and naming\n\n- Files `test_*.py`, functions `test_*`, one behavior per test. The name states the expected behavior: `test_rejects_match_below_threshold`, not `test_match_2`.\n- **Arrange / Act / Assert** with blank lines between phases. If a test needs comments to explain phases, it is doing too much.\n- Put shared fixtures in `conftest.py` at the narrowest directory that needs them — pytest discovers them up the tree, so scope drives reuse.\n\n## Fixtures over setUp\n\nFixtures are dependency injection for tests: request what you need, get teardown for free via `yield`.\n\n```python\nimport pytest\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef settings(tmp_path):\n    # tmp_path is a per-test directory — no manual cleanup, no shared state\n    return Settings(database_file=str(tmp_path / \"test.db\"))\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef repo(settings):\n    conn = open_connection(settings.database_file)\n    run_migrations(conn)\n    yield Repository(conn)   # everything after yield is teardown\n    conn.close()\n```\n\nScope deliberately: default `function` (fresh per test, safest). Use `module`/`session` only for expensive, read-only setup — shared mutable fixtures leak state and create order-dependent flakiness.\n\n## Parametrize instead of loops\n\nA loop inside one test stops at the first failure and reports one case. `parametrize` runs each case independently and names it.\n\n```python\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"title_a\", \"title_b\", \"expected\"),\n    [\n        (\"Song (Live)\", \"Song\", True),\n        (\"Song\", \"Totally Other\", False),\n    ],\n    ids=[\"live-suffix-matches\", \"different-titles-reject\"],\n)\ndef test_fuzzy_match(title_a, title_b, expected):\n    assert is_match(title_a, title_b) is expected\n```\n\n## Async tests (pytest-asyncio)\n\nWhen `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"`, every `async def test_*` runs on the event loop with no decorator. Without it, mark each one `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. Know which mode the repo uses before adding tests.\n\n```toml\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\nasyncio_mode = \"auto\"\n```\n\n```python\nasync def test_fetches_playlist(httpx_mock):\n    httpx_mock.add_response(json={\"items\": []})\n    result = await client.get_playlist(\"abc\")\n    assert result == []\n```\n\nAsync fixtures use the same `async def` + `yield` shape. Do not call `asyncio.run()` inside a test — you are already on the loop; nesting raises `RuntimeError`.\n\n## Mocking — at the boundary, not the internals\n\nMock I/O and external services (YouTube/Spotify APIs, the network), not your own pure functions. Prefer real objects (the `tmp_path` SQLite DB) over mocks when they are cheap — sortarr's web tests run against a real in-process SQLite DB for exactly this reason.\n\n```python\ndef test_skips_on_api_error(monkeypatch):\n    def boom(*_): raise TimeoutError\n    monkeypatch.setattr(client, \"get_playlist\", boom)\n    # monkeypatch auto-reverts after the test — no manual cleanup\n```\n\n- `monkeypatch` for attributes/env/dicts (auto-reverted).\n- `unittest.mock.AsyncMock` for awaitables; a plain `Mock` returns a coroutine-less value and the `await` fails.\n- For httpx, prefer `pytest-httpx`'s `httpx_mock` or `respx` over patching internals — patch the transport, not the call site.\n\n## Coverage and CI\n\n```bash\npytest                       # all tests\npytest -k \"match and not slow\"   # filter by name expression\npytest -x --ff               # stop at first failure, failed-first ordering\npytest -q tests/test_match.py::test_fuzzy_match   # one test\npytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing        # coverage with missing lines\n```\n\nCoverage is a floor, not a goal: 100% coverage with no assertions tests nothing. Chase uncovered *branches* that carry risk, not the percentage.\n\n## Targeted mutation testing\n\nAfter the relevant suite is green, consider a few mutations for changed or high-risk comparisons, guards, exception paths, and state updates. Mutation testing changes production code to challenge the tests; coverage only shows execution. Neither a whole-repository run nor a fixed mutation score is required.\n\n**Manual fallback:** preserve current edits and use an isolated test copy containing the candidate. Run the selected pytest cases and confirm they actually collected and passed rather than only skipping/xfailing. Change one production behavior with tests fixed, rerun, and inspect the failing assertion. Verify imports resolve to the mutated source, not another installed package or a monkeypatched replacement. An import/setup/type-check failure or unexplained timeout is not an assertion-based kill. For a real survivor, add a contract-derived test and prove it rejects the mutant. Restore only the probe change, inspect the diff, and rerun the relevant suite without discarding unrelated work.\n\n**Automation:** [mutmut](https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is an option for a compatible pytest project. Prefer the repository's pinned environment. Check the installed version's help and documentation before choosing source paths, test selection, timeout/concurrency settings, or configuration keys; these can differ between versions. Bound the scope before using `mutmut run`, then inspect outcomes with `mutmut browse`. Verify copied fixtures/configuration and imported source. Do not treat cached/incremental results as a fresh run when dependencies, configuration, fixtures, or the candidate changed without the tool accounting for them.\n\n`mutmut apply` writes a mutant into source. Use it only in an isolated, recoverable copy and verify restoration even after interruption. Do not install tools or publish reports merely because the command appears here; a safe manual sample or a stated limitation is preferable to unsupported setup.\n\nRecord candidate, tool/Python versions, source/test scope, budget, baseline, actual outcomes, and final restoration in existing verification notes. Triage survivors into real gaps, missing execution, justified equivalence/out-of-scope behavior, or unresolved cases. Keep invalid/timeout/error/untested outcomes visible and report any score with its definition and denominator. Never weaken expected values, skip a hard test, or add an unjustified exclusion to raise that score. `test-driven-development` contains the shared method and deeper triage guidance.\n\n## Common mistakes\n\n| Mistake | Fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| `async def` test with no `asyncio_mode`/marker | Test is silently skipped or errors. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` or mark it. |\n| `Mock()` where an `await` happens | Use `AsyncMock`; a sync Mock isn't awaitable. |\n| `session`-scoped mutable fixture | Tests leak state and depend on order. Default to `function` scope. |\n| Loop over cases in one test | Use `parametrize` so each case runs and reports independently. |\n| Mocking your own pure logic | Mock only I/O boundaries; test real logic directly. |\n| Shared session/file DB across tests | Give each test its own DB via `tmp_path` (function scope); a shared file leaks state and throws `database is locked` under parallel workers. |\n| `assertEqual`/`TestCase` boilerplate | Use plain `assert`; pytest rewrites it with rich diffs. |\n\n## References\n\n- [pytest documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/)\n- [pytest-asyncio](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/)\n- [pytest-httpx](https://github.com/Colin-b/pytest_httpx)\n\nBase directory for this skill: /workspace/.opencode/skills/python-testing\nRelative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\nNote: file list is sampled.\n\n<skill_files>\n</skill_files>\n</skill_content>"
